{{short description|Swedish physicist}}
{{For|other people with the same name|Sven Nilsson (disambiguation){{!}}Sven Nilsson}}
'''Sven Gösta Nilsson''' (January 14, 1927, Kristianstad – April 24, 1979, Lund) was a Swedish [[theoretical physicist]] at the [[Lund Institute of Technology]].

Nilsson's father was a preacher. As an undergraduate engineering student, he spent a year at Occidental College in California. He obtained a Master of Science in [[engineering physics]] at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] in [[Stockholm]]. Influenced by [[Tommy Lauritsen]] and [[Torsten Gustafson]], Nilsson decided to switch paths from engineering to physics, and in 1950 he was admitted to postgraduate studies in Lund with Gustafson as his supervisor.

After early work with Lauritsen on [[Nuclear isomer|excited states]] in [[Lithium-6|<sup>6</sup>Li]], Nilsson became interested in evidence that heavy [[atomic nucleus|nuclei]] could be deformed into [[ellipsoidal]] rather than spherical shapes. Rotational bands had been discovered in 1953, an observation that was incompatible with a spherically symmetric shape.

Nilsson set out  to produce a model for the structure of deformed nuclei, building on work by [[Maria Goeppert-Mayer]] that had been published in 1950, as well as work by [[Aage Bohr]] and [[Ben Mottelson]] at the Institute for Theoretical Physics (later the [[Niels Bohr Institute]]). His research, in collaboration with Bohr and Mottelson, led to the so-called [[Nilsson model]] and a 1955 doctoral thesis, "On some properties of nuclear states."<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=On some properties of nuclear states |url=https://lubcat.lub.lu.se/cgi-bin/koha/opac-detail.pl?biblionumber=7120758 |publisher=förf. |date=1955 |place=Lund |first=Sven Gösta |last=Nilsson}}</ref> Nilsson's main innovations were the introduction of a method for modeling the flat-bottomed shape of the nuclear potential, as well as formulating a model that made calculations practical, and exploiting the digital computing technology of the day.

Nilsson and Mottelson  embarked on a comprehensive program of comparing nuclear properties with the predictions of the deformed shell model. The Nilsson model was successful in explaining the [[Spin (physics)|spins]] and [[Nuclear magnetic moment|magnetic moments]] of nuclei far from [[Nuclear shell model|closed shells]], problems which would have been intractable with the spherical shell model. In many cases, a disagreement between theory and experiment led to the discovery that the experimental results had been mistaken.

Sven Gösta Nilsson was involved in the work of [[CERN]]'s Theoretical Study Division when the group was located in Copenhagen.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mottelson |first1=B. R. |last2=Nilsson |first2=S. G. |date=1955-09-01 |title=Classification of the Nucleonic States in Deformed Nuclei |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.99.1615 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=99 |issue=5 |pages=1615–1617 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.99.1615 |bibcode=1955PhRv...99.1615M |issn=0031-899X}}</ref> More than twenty years later, then in [[Geneva]], he spent a sabbatical period at CERN.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Andersson |first1=C.G. |last2=Hellström |first2=G. |last3=Leander |first3=G. |last4=Ragnarsson |first4=I. |last5=Åberg |first5=S. |last6=Krumlinde |first6=J. |last7=Nilsson |first7=S.G. |last8=Szymański |first8=Z. |date=1978-10-16 |title=Islands of high-spin yrast isomers |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0375947478905407 |journal=Nuclear Physics A |language=en |volume=309 |issue=1–2 |pages=141–176 |doi=10.1016/0375-9474(78)90540-7|bibcode=1978NuPhA.309..141A |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Starting in 1963, he was a professor of mathematical physics at the two-year-old Lund University of Technology, helping to build its research programs. In 1974 he was elected to membership in the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. He was an active environmentalist and frequent author of newspaper articles. Nilsson is buried at [[Norra kyrkogården]] in Lund.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mottelson |first=Ben |date=2006-06-01 |title=The Nilsson Model and Sven Gösta Nilsson |journal=Physica Scripta |volume=T125 |doi=10.1088/1402-4896/2006/T125/E02 |issn=0031-8949|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sven Gösta Nilsson and his Model {{!}} PHYSICS IN LUND |url=http://history.fysik.lu.se/images/FysicumsHistoriaBok_pdf/EN_PhysicsInLund_web/EN_Bok_12_SGN_web.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526213806/http://history.fysik.lu.se/images/FysicumsHistoriaBok_pdf/EN_PhysicsInLund_web/EN_Bok_12_SGN_web.pdf |archive-date=26 May 2019 |access-date=7 June 2022 |website=www.fysik.lu.se }}</ref>
